Character Type: N Maximum Length: 6 bytes 
 
Representation: Fixed length of six digits 
Purpose: Note: Identifies a transaction for the life of the transaction. 
Sequence Number must persist in all the subsequent transactions 
that are associated with the initial authorization request. 
 In the case of a preauthorized transaction, the Sequence Number 
in the Purchase/Capture identifies the Sequence Number in the 
transaction’s Authorization Only request. 
Processing Rules: Each transaction has a unique Sequence Number.  It is included 
on all transaction types, and originates at the device. 
 In the case of a preauthorized transaction, the Sequence Number 
in the Purchase/Capture is the same Sequence Number as in the 
transaction’s Authorization Only request. 
 In the case of a purchase reversal/void or time-out reversal 
transaction, the Sequence Number must be the same as in the 
original transaction request. 
 In the case of an Authorization Only Reversal, this element—
present in the original transaction—must be present and identical 
in the Authorization Only Reversal transaction.  (Note:  The 
Authorization Only Reversal transaction enables a merchant to 
reverse the following credit card transactions within required 
timeframes:  POS Authorization Only [Transaction Type code 
“3”]); POS Mail/Phone Authorization Only [Transaction Type code 
“B”]); and CAT Authorization Only [Transaction Type code “5”]). 
 For TransArmor PKI Encryption and Tokenization, this element is 
included in a new data segment (No. 116 [TransArmor Load Data 
Segment]).

Appendix X-1 
 
Appendix X.  Online Refund/Refund Authorization 
Note: Please contact your First Data representative for availability of this functionality 
Today, cardholders have real-time, 24/7 access to their online banking apps through 
smartphones and other devices. They are more aware than ever of how quickly purchase 
information is updated to their account. However, cardholders also have become increasingly 
aware that the same flow of information does not exist on purchase returns. 
To align the purchase and return processes, an authorization was introduced on credit voucher 
(aka purchase return) transactions. This new credit voucher / purchase return authorization 
message will provide issuers with real-time information about returns, similar to that for 
purchases, which they must then provide to their cardholders.  
Merchants must send the Online Refund/Refund Authorization Indicator in Sub-table ID 11 of 
POS Additional Data Information (Table ID 32) in Appendix I (Variable Information Data 
Layouts) when participating in Online Refund/Refund Authorization program to get authorization 
for Merchandise Return transactions. Merchants who do not want Merchandise Return to be 
approved online must not send this field. 
The value of the Online Refund/Refund Authorization Indicator should be ‘Y’ for Visa, 
MasterCard, Amex, and Discover. 
When the Online Refund/Refund Authorization Indicator is included in a Merchandise Return 
transaction, this indicator should also be included in the subsequent reversal/follow-up 
transactions and Timeout reversals. 
Starting October, 2018, for certain merchants Visa will require a ‘real-time’ message using the 
Authorization system, prior to an existing Settlement System Refund. Impacted merchants have 
already been notified. All other merchants are expected to perform Visa online authorization 
effective April, 2020..  
A ‘real time’ message (like an Authorization) will advise the issuer and/or cardholder that a 
refund is pending. This will help to eliminate the delay between the merchant deciding to initiate 
a Refund and the visible impact on the cardholder’s account. 
It is expected that an Online Refund/Refund Authorization will only be declined if the Issuer 
cannot be reached or the cardholder account is not valid; however declining transactions for any 
reason is subject to the Issuer’s discretion.

Appendix AF-1 
 
Appendix AF. Estimated and Incremental 
Authorization Transactions 
 
The Incremental Auth product is a means for a merchant to open an authorization, and modify it 
over time, before eventually submitting the final amount in the form of completion.  This 
functionality has typically been used in the lodging and car rental industries, where the Initial 
Authorization may occur days before the transaction is completed, but is being expanded to 
support additional industries.  
 
The Incremental Auth (IA) product supports four transaction types: 
• Original Auth (aka Estimated Auth) 
• Incremental Auth 
• Partial Reversal (aka IA Reversal) 
• Incremental Auth Completion (aka IA Completion) 
 
This functionality is mandatory for Discover and is not limited by MCC. 
For Visa, Mastercard, and American Express, the use of this functionality is strongly 
recommended in addition to populating the Estimated and Incremental Authorization fields for 
the applicable lodging and EV transactions. 
 
REQUIREMENTS:  
• All IA transaction types should contain Incremental Auth Data (Variable Information 
segment 111 Table 82).  This is mandatory for Discover. 
o Incremental Auth Data contains the Transaction ID which must be unique (per 
terminal) to any open Incremental Auth purchase. 
• Incremental Auths, IA Reversals, and IA Completions are all subsequent transactions, 
and must be preceded by an Original Auth. 
• Subsequent IA transactions must contain the Approval Code (DE 39) that was received 
on the approved Original Auth. 
• Once an IA Completion is received, the IA is closed, and no more subsequent 
transactions will be approved for that Terminal Transaction ID.
